Ok(())\n425\t    }\n426\t}\n427\t\n428\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n429\t// Built-in adapters\n430\t// };\n1462\t\n1463\t            outcome\n1464\t        };\n1465\t\n1466\t        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.agent.exit_code\", exit_code);\n1467\t\n1468\t        // Set span status: Ok for self.timeout_secs\n        } else {\n            global_timeout_secs\n        };\n        if secs == 0 {\n            Duration::ZERO\n        } else {\n            Duration::from_secs(secs)\n \"anthropic\", \"openai\", \"local\").\n    /// Defaults to \"local\" if no provider is configured.\n    pub fn gen_ai_system(&self) -> &str {\n        self.provider.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"local\")\n    }\n\n    /// Active timeout policy for this adapter.\n    ///\n    /// Distinguishes between legacy single timeout and the new two-field\n    /// (idle + hard) timeout model.\n    pub fn timeout_policy(&self) -> TimeoutPolicy {\n        let has_legacy = self.timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_idle = self.idle_timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_hard = self.hard_timeout_secs > 0;\n\n        if has_legacy {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Legacy\n        } else if has_idle || has_hard {\n            TimeoutPolicy::New {\n                idle_enabled: has_idle,\n                hard_enabled: has_hard,\n            }\n        } else {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Global\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Human-readable description of the active timeout policy.\n    ///\n    /// Shows which timeout mode is active and the configured values.\n    pub fn timeout_description(&self, global_timeout_secs: u64) -> String {\n        match self.timeout_policy() {\n            TimeoutPolicy::Legacy => {\n                format!(\"legacy: {}s (single timeout)\", self.timeout_secs)\n            }\n            TimeoutPolicy::New {\n                idle_enabled,\n                hard_enabled,\n            } => {\n                let mut parts = Vec::new();\n                parts.push(\"new:\".to_string());\n                if idle_enabled {\n                    parts.push(format!(\"idle={}s\", self.idle_timeout_secs));\n                }\n                if hard_enabled {\n                    parts.push(format!(\"hard={}s\", self.hard_timeout_secs));\n                }\n                if !idle_enabled && !hard_enabled {\n                    parts.push(\"both disabled\".to_string());\n                }\n                parts.join(\" \")\n            }\n            TimeoutPolicy::Global => {\n                if global_timeout_secs > 0 {\n                    format!(\"global: {}s (from config)\", global_timeout_secs)\n                } else {\n                    \"global: unlimited (0 = no timeout)\".to_string()\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Validate timeout field mutual exclusivity.\n    ///\n    /// Legacy `timeout_secs` and new `idle_timeout_secs`/`hard_timeout_secs`\n    /// cannot both be set. This preserves backward compatibility while allowing\n    /// the new two-field timeout model.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - `timeout_secs` is non-zero AND either `idle_timeout_secs` or `hard_timeout_secs` is non-zero\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// // Valid: legacy timeout alone\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_timeout_secs_only().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Valid: new timeout fields together\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_new_timeouts().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Valid: new timeout field alone (other set to 0)\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_idle_only().validate_timeouts().is_ok());\n    ///\n    /// // Invalid: mixing legacy and new\n    /// assert!(adapter_with_mixed_timeouts().validate_timeouts().is_err());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn validate_timeouts(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let has_legacy = self.timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_idle = self.idle_timeout_secs > 0;\n        let has_hard = self.hard_timeout_secs > 0;\n\n        if has_legacy && (has_idle || has_hard) {\n            bail!(\n                \"adapter '{}' has incompatible timeout configuration: \\\n                 legacy field 'timeout_secs' ({}) cannot be used together with new fields \\\n                 'idle_timeout_secs' ({}) or 'hard_timeout_secs' ({}). \\\n                 Use either timeout_secs alone (legacy) or idle_timeout_secs + hard_timeout_secs (new).\",\n                self.name,\n                self.timeout_secs,\n                self.idle_timeout_secs,\n                self.hard_timeout_secs\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Built-in adapters\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Template rendering\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Substitute known variables in an invoke template.\nfn render_template(\n    template: &str,\n    workspace: &Path,\n    prompt_file: &Path,\n    bead_id: &BeadId,\n    model: &str,\n) -> String {\n    template\n        .replace(\"{workspace}\", &workspace.display().to_string())\n        .replace(\"{prompt_file}\", &prompt_file.display().to_string())\n        .replace(\"{bead_id}\", bead_id.as_ref())\n        .replace(\"{model}\", model)\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Adapter loading\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Load adapters from YAML files, with built-in defaults.\n///\n/// Built-in adapters are loaded first; user files in `dir` override by name.\npub fn load_adapters(\n    dir: &Path,\n    built_ins: &[AgentAdapter],\n) -> Result<HashMap<String, AgentAdapter>> {\n    let mut adapters = HashMap::new();\n\n    for adapter in built_ins {\n        adapters.insert(adapter.name.clone(), adapter.clone());\n    }\n\n    if dir.exists() && dir.is_dir() {\n        let entries = std::fs::read_dir(dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read adapters dir: {}\", dir.display()))?;\n\n        for entry in entries {\n            let entry = entry?;\n            let path = entry.path();\n            let is_yaml = path\n                .extension()\n                .is_some_and(|ext| ext == \"yaml\" || ext == \"yml\");\n            if is_yaml {\n                let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read adapter file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n                let adapter: AgentAdapter = serde_yaml::from_str(&text)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid YAML in adapter file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n\n                // Validate timeout field mutual exclusivity\n                adapter.validate_timeouts().with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\n                        \"adapter '{}' in file {} has invalid timeout configuration\",\n                        adapter.name,\n                        path.display()\n                    )\n                })?;\n\n                adapters.insert(adapter.name.clone(), adapter);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Log timeout policy for all loaded adapters\n    let global_timeout = 3600; // Default, will be overridden by dispatcher\n    for adapter in adapters.values() {\n        let policy = adapter.timeout_policy();\n        let desc = adapter.timeout_description(global_timeout);\n        tracing::debug!(\n            adapter = %adapter.name,\n            timeout_policy = ?policy,\n            timeout_config = %desc,\n            \"loaded adapter with timeout configuration\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    Ok(adapters)\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Dispatcher\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Executes agent processes for claimed beads.\npub struct Dispatcher {\n    adapters: HashMap<String, AgentAdapter>,\n    telemetry: Telemetry,\n    global_timeout_secs: u64,\n    /// Sanitizer applied to all trace content before writing to disk.\n    /// `None` when trace sanitization is disabled in config.\n    sanitizer: Option<Arc<Sanitizer>>,\n    /// Tsnet identity registry for per-worker network identity.\n    /// `None` when tsnet is disabled in config.\n    tsnet_registry: Option<IdentityRegistry>,\n    /// Tsnet configuration (cached from config).\n    tsnet_config: TsnetConfig,\n}\n\nimpl Dispatcher {\n    /// Create a new dispatcher, loading adapters from config.\n    pub fn new(config: &Config, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Result<Self> {\n        let adapters = load_adapters(&config.agent.adapters_dir, &builtin_adapters())?;\n        let sanitizer = build_sanitizer(config);\n        let tsnet_config = config.tsnet.clone();\n\n        // Create tsnet registry only if enabled\n        let tsnet_registry = if tsnet_config.enabled {\n            Some(IdentityRegistry::new(tsnet_config.clone()))\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        Ok(Dispatcher {\n            adapters,\n            telemetry,\n            global_timeout_secs: config.agent.timeout,\n            sanitizer,\n            tsnet_registry,\n            tsnet_config,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Create a dispatcher with explicit adapters (for testing).\n    pub fn with_adapters(\n        adapters: HashMap<String, AgentAdapter>,\n        telemetry: Telemetry,\n        global_timeout_secs: u64,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Dispatcher {\n            adapters,\n            telemetry,\n            global_timeout_secs,\n            sanitizer: None,\n            tsnet_registry: None,\n            tsnet_config: TsnetConfig::default(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Look up an adapter by name.\n    pub fn adapter(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&AgentAdapter> {\n        self.adapters.get(name)\n    }\n\n    /// List all loaded adapter names.\n    pub fn adapter_names(&self) -> Vec<&str> {\n        self.adapters.keys().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve an adapter name from a model name using routing rules.\n    ///\n    /// If routing is configured in the config, returns the adapter name that\n    /// matches the model pattern (first match wins). Otherwise, returns the\n    /// default adapter name.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `model` - Model name (e.g., \"sonnet\", \"claude-opus-4-8\", \"fable\")\n    /// * `config` - Full config containing routing rules\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    /// The resolved adapter name (e.g., \"claude-code-glm-4.7\", \"claude-sonnet\")\n    pub fn resolve_adapter_name(&self, model: &str, config: &Config) -> String {\n        if let Some(ref routing) = config.agent.routing {\n            // Check each routing rule in order (first match wins)\n            for rule in &routing.rules {\n                match regex::Regex::new(&rule.match_model) {\n                    Ok(re) => {\n                        if re.is_match(model) {\n                            tracing::debug!(\n                                model = %model,\n                                pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                                adapter = %rule.adapter,\n                                \"routing rule matched\"\n                            );\n                            return rule.adapter.clone();\n                        }\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        // Regex was validated during config load, so this should never happen.\n                        // Fall back to default if somehow we get an invalid pattern at runtime.\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                            \"invalid routing regex pattern (should have been caught by config validation)\"\n                        );\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // No rules matched; use default_adapter if set\n            if let Some(ref default_adapter) = routing.default_adapter {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    model = %model,\n                    adapter = %default_adapter,\n                    \"no routing rules matched, using default_adapter\"\n                );\n                return default_adapter.clone();\n            }\n        }\n\n        // No routing configured or no default_adapter; fall back to agent.default\n        tracing::debug!(\n            model = %model,\n            adapter = %config.agent.default,\n            \"no routing configured, using agent.default\"\n        );\n        config.agent.default.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Execute the agent process for a bead.\n    ///\n    /// 1. Writes the prompt to a temp file\n    /// 2. Renders the invoke template with variables\n    /// 3. Sets adapter-specific environment variables\n    /// 4. Spawns the process via `bash -c`\n    /// 5. Waits with timeout enforcement (kills on timeout, exit 124)\n    /// 6. Captures stdout, stderr, exit code\n    /// 7. Cleans up the temp file\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"agent.dispatch\",\n        skip(self, bead_id, prompt, adapter, workspace),\n        fields(\n            needle.bead.id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n            gen_ai.system = %adapter.gen_ai_system(),\n            gen_ai.operation.name = \"chat\",\n            gen_ai.request.id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n            needle.agent.pid = tracing::field::Empty,\n            needle.agent.exit_code = tracing::field::Empty,\n        )\n    )]\n    pub async fn dispatch(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        prompt: &BuiltPrompt,\n        adapter: &AgentAdapter,\n        workspace: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult> {\n        // Set gen_ai.request.model if available\n        if let Some(ref model) = adapter.model {\n            tracing::Span::current().record(\"gen_ai.request.model\", model.as_str());\n        }\n\n        // Log timeout policy for this dispatch\n        let timeout_policy = adapter.timeout_policy();\n        let timeout_desc = adapter.timeout_description(self.global_timeout_secs);\n        tracing::debug!(\n            adapter = %adapter.name,\n            timeout_policy = ?timeout_policy,\n            timeout_config = %timeout_desc,\n            \"dispatching agent with timeout policy\"\n        );\n\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::DispatchStarted {\n            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n            agent: adapter.name.clone(),\n            prompt_len: prompt.content.len(),\n            template_name: prompt.template_name.clone(),\n            template_version: prompt.template_version.clone(),\n            prompt_hash: prompt.hash.clone(),\n        })?;\n\n        let result = self\n            .execute_agent(bead_id, &prompt.content, adapter, workspace)\n            .await;\n\n        // Emit completion telemetry regardless of success/failure.\n        let agent_name = adapter.name.clone();\n        let agent_model = adapter.model.clone();\n        match &result {\n            Ok(exec) => {\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.agent.pid\", exec.pid);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.agent.exit_code\", exec.exit_code);\n\n                // Extract token usage and set gen_ai.usage attributes\n                let usage = extract_tokens(&adapter.token_extraction, &exec.stdout, &exec.stderr);\n                if let Some(input_tokens) = usage.input_tokens {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens\", input_tokens);\n                }\n                if let Some(output_tokens) = usage.output_tokens {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"gen_ai.usage.output_tokens\", output_tokens);\n                }\n\n                // Set span status: Ok for exit_code 0, Error otherwise\n                if exec.exit_code != 0 {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\n                        \"otel.status_description\",\n                        format!(\"exit_code: {}\", exec.exit_code),\n                    );\n                }\n\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::DispatchCompleted {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    exit_code: exec.exit_code,\n                    duration_ms: exec.elapsed.as_millis() as u64,\n                    agent: agent_name,\n                    model: agent_model,\n                });\n\n                // Emit structured timeout event if applicable.\n                if let Some(ref reason) = exec.timeout_reason {\n                    let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::AgentTimeout {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: reason.clone(),\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                // Set span status on error\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", \"dispatch_error\");\n\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::DispatchCompleted {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    exit_code: -1,\n                    duration_ms: 0,\n                    agent: agent_name,\n                    model: agent_model,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        result\n    }\n\n    /// Internal: execute the agent, ensuring temp file cleanup.\n    async fn execute_agent(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        prompt_content: &str,\n        adapter: &AgentAdapter,\n        workspace: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult> {\n        let prompt_file = write_prompt_to_temp(bead_id, prompt_content)?;\n\n        let result = self\n            .run_process(bead_id, adapter, workspace, &prompt_file)\n            .await;\n\n        // Always clean up temp file.\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&prompt_file);\n\n        result\n    }\n\n    /// Internal: spawn and manage the agent process.\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"agent.execution\",\n        skip(self, bead_id, adapter, workspace, prompt_file),\n        fields(\n            needle.bead.id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n            needle.agent.pid = tracing::field::Empty,\n            needle.agent.exit_code = tracing::field::Empty,\n        )\n    )]\n    async fn run_process(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        adapter: &AgentAdapter,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        prompt_file: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<ExecutionResult> {\n        // Create trace capture for this bead execution.\n        // Sanitizer is cloned (Arc clone — cheap) and applied before every disk write.\n        let trace_capture =\n            TraceCapture::new_with_sanitizer(bead_id, workspace, self.sanitizer.clone());\n\n        // Provision tsnet identity if enabled\n        let worker_id = self.telemetry.worker_id().to_string();\n        let tsnet_identity = if let Some(ref registry) = self.tsnet_registry {\n            match registry.provision_identity(&worker_id, bead_id).await {\n                Ok(identity) => Some(identity),\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        worker_id = %worker_id,\n                        bead_id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to provision tsnet identity, continuing without network identity\"\n                    );\n                    None\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        let model = adapter.model.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"default\");\n        let rendered = render_template(\n            &adapter.invoke_template,\n            workspace,\n            prompt_file,\n            bead_id,\n            model,\n        );\n\n        // Build environment variables for the child process\n        let mut child_env = adapter.environment.clone();\n\n        // Inject tsnet identity environment variables if provisioned\n        if let (Some(ref identity), Some(_)) = (&tsnet_identity, &self.tsnet_registry) {\n            inject_identity_env(identity, &self.tsnet_config, &mut child_env);\n        }\n\n        // Spawn the agent process with ETXTBSY retry handling.\n        // This wrapper retries with backoff if the kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26),\n        // which can occur when a binary has been written to disk and immediately executed.\n        let rendered_clone = rendered.clone();\n        let child_env_clone = child_env.clone();\n        let adapter_name_clone = adapter.name.clone();\n        let mut child = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_child(\n            || {\n                let rendered = rendered_clone.clone();\n                let child_env = child_env_clone.clone();\n                let adapter_name = adapter_name_clone.clone();\n                async move {\n                    // Safety: setpgid(0,0) is async-signal-safe and idempotent.\n                    unsafe {\n                        tokio::process::Command::new(\"bash\")\n                            .arg(\"-c\")\n                            .arg(&rendered)\n                            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                            .envs(&child_env)\n                     // try_send drops lines when the transform is\n                                // slower than the agent.\n                                let (tx, mut rx) =                       // transform stdin. // writing and closing stdin before deciding\n                                // whether the transform deserves a kill.\n                                let feeder_task = tokio::spawn(async move {\n // Compute per-bead log file path.\n                                let log_path = agent_log_path(self.telemetry.worker_id(), bead_id);\n\n                                // Log writer task: reads ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Compute the per-bead agent log path: `~/.needle/logs/<worker>-<bead_id>.agent.jsonl`.\n///\n/// Build a trace sanitizer from the workspace config.\n///\n/// Returns `None` if sanitization is disabled or if rule compilation fails\n/// (failing open keeps traces writable even when the sanitizer has issues).\nfn build_sanitizer(config: &Config) -> Option<Arc<Sanitizer>> {\n    if }\n277\t\n278\t    /// Handle a process output with cancellation support.\n279\t    ///\n280\t    /// Checks the cancellation flag before starting the handler and returns\n281\t    /// early if the .map(|(name, r)| (name.clone(), r.failure_reason().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string()))\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| (\"unknown\".to_string(), \"unknown error\".to_string()));\n\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            gate = %failed_gate,\n            reason = %reason,\n            \"validation gate failed — releasing bead\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit verification failure telemetry.\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::VerificationFailed {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            command: failed_gate.clone(),\n            exit_code: None,\n            output: reason,\n        })?;\n\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // If the agent already closed the bead, reopen it before releasing.\n        // Use timeout to prevent indefinite hang in HANDLING state.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.show(&bead.id), \"show\").await {\n            Ok(Some(current)) if current.status.is_done() => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"reopening bead closed by agent (verification failed)\"\n                );\n                match self.timeout_op(|| store.reopen(&bead.id), \"reopen\").await {\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to reopen bead — attempting release anyway\"\n                        );\n                        events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                            outcome: \"gate_failure\".to_string(),\n                            operation: \"reopen\".to_string(),\n                            error: e.to_string(),\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"show() timed out during gate failure handling, skipping reopen\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"gate_failure\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"show() failed during gate failure handling\"\n                );\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n\n        // Release the bead back to open with flush-before-release and sync recovery.\n        let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        events.append(&mut release_events);\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment the failure count and apply the same\n        // quarantine ceiling `handle_failure` uses. Without this, a bead that\n        // fails a gate every cycle is released back to open forever: the\n        // ARMOR/bf-135k storm ran one bead 24 times in a single day, each\n        // attempt leaving another commit behind. A gate failure is no less\n        // repeatable than an agent failure and must respect the same ceiling.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        let mut action = BeadAction::Released;\n        if release_succeeded {\n            match self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                Ok(new_count) => {\n                    let threshold = self.config.outcome.quarantine_after_failures;\n                    if threshold > 0 && new_count >= threshold {\n                        match self\n                            .quarantine_bead(store, bead, new_count, threshold)\n                            .await\n                        {\n                            Ok(quarantine_events) => {\n                                events.extend(quarantine_events);\n                                action = BeadAction::Quarantined;\n                            }\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                tracing::warn!(\n                                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                    error = %e,\n                                    \"failed to quarantine bead after exceeding gate-failure threshold\"\n                                );\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to increment failure count after gate failure\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add a label indicating verification failure.\n        if let Err(e) = tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, \"verification-failed\"),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to add verification-failed label\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok((action, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Failure: release bead and increment failure count.\n    ///\n    /// Mitosis evaluation (for multi-task splitting) is handled externally by\n    /// the worker after outcome handling — see `MitosisEvaluator`.\n    ///\n    /// If br calls timeout or fail, logs the error and continues — does not\n    /// block the worker in HANDLING state indefinitely.\n    async fn handle_failure(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent failure — releasing bead\");\n\n        let mut events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count and check the\n        // quarantine threshold. A bead that has exceeded\n        // `outcome.quarantine_after_failures` consecutive failures is\n        // quarantined (status=blocked) instead of being left released-to-open\n        // for the next cycle to re-claim and fail again indefinitely. This\n        // also closes the mitosis `NotSplittable` fallthrough (worker/mod.rs):\n        // that verdict no longer matters for beads at or past the ceiling,\n        // since this check already ran before mitosis evaluation this cycle.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        let mut action = BeadAction::Released;\n        if release_succeeded {\n            match self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                Ok(new_count) => {\n                    let threshold = self.config.outcome.quarantine_after_failures;\n                    if threshold > 0 && new_count >= threshold {\n                        match self\n                            .quarantine_bead(store, bead, new_count, threshold)\n                            .await\n                        {\n                            Ok(quarantine_events) => {\n                                events.extend(quarantine_events);\n                                action = BeadAction::Quarantined;\n                            }\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                tracing::warn!(\n                                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                    error = %e,\n                                    \"failed to quarantine bead after exceeding failure threshold\"\n                                );\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to increment failure count after release\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Ensure we emit a reason event for telemetry.\n        if !events.iter().any(|e| {\n            matches!(\n                e,\n                EventKind::BeadReleased { .. } | EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { .. }\n            )\n        }) {\n            events.push(EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                reason: \"failure\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        Ok((action, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Timeout: release bead and add `deferred` label.\n    ///\n    /// If br calls timeout or fail, logs the error and continues — does not\n    /// block the worker in HANDLING state indefinitely.\n    async fn handle_timeout(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent timed out — releasing bead as deferred\");\n\n        let mut events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count and add deferred label.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        if release_succeeded {\n            // Increment failure count for auto-split tracking.\n            if let Err(e) = self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to increment failure count after timeout\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            if let Err(e) = tokio::time::timeout(\n                std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                store.add_label(&bead.id, \"deferred\"),\n            )\n            .await\n            {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"add_label deferred timed out or failed after timeout release\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"timeout\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Deferred, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Crash: release bead and create alert bead with diagnostic info.\n    async fn handle_crash(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        signal_code: i32,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::error!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            signal_code,\n            agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            \"agent crashed — releasing bead and creating alert\"\n        );\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // Create alert bead with diagnostic info (best-effort).\n        let signal_num = if signal_code > 128 {\n            signal_code - 128\n        } else {\n            signal_code\n        };\n        let timestamp = Utc::now().to_rfc3339();\n        let alert_title = format!(\"ALERT: Agent crash on bead {}\", bead.id);\n        let alert_body = format!(\n            \"## Agent Crash Report\\n\\\n             \\n\\\n             - **Bead ID**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Agent**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Exit code**: {} (signal {})\\n\\\n             - **Workspace**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Timestamp**: {}\\n\\\n             \\n\\\n             The agent process was killed. This bead has been released for retry.\",\n            bead.id,\n            self.config.agent.default,\n            signal_code,\n            signal_num,\n            bead.workspace.display(),\n            timestamp,\n        );\n\n        // Hook 4: propagate stitch labels from the crashed bead to the alert.\n        let signal_label = format!(\"signal-{}\", signal_num);\n        let mut alert_labels: Vec<String> = vec![\"alert\".into(), \"crash\".into(), signal_label];\n        alert_labels.extend(crate::types::extract_stitch_labels(&bead.labels));\n        let alert_label_refs: Vec<&str> = alert_labels.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.create_bead(&alert_title, &alert_body, &alert_label_refs),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(alert_id)) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    %alert_id,\n                    \"crash alert bead created\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to create crash alert bead\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"create_bead timed out after 30s during crash handling\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Alerted, events))\n    }\n\n    /// AgentNotFound: release bead, emit error. No retry — this is a config issue.\n    async fn handle_agent_not_found(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::error!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            \"agent binary not found — releasing bead (config issue, no retry)\"\n        );\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Interrupted: release bead for graceful shutdown.\n    async fn handle_interrupted(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent interrupted — releasing bead for clean shutdown\");\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Increment the failure count label on a bead.\n    ///\n    /// Labels follow the pattern `failure-count:N`. If `failure-count:2` exists,\n    /// the old label is removed and `failure-count:3` is added.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the new failure count (or 0 if the operation failed).\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn increment_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<u32> {\n        // Read labels with timeout.\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(&bead.id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"could not read labels to increment failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, skipping failure count increment\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n            };\n\n        let current_count = labels\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(\"failure-count:\"))\n            .filter_map(|n| n.parse::<u32>().ok())\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        let new_count = current_count + 1;\n        let new_label = format!(\"failure-count:{}\", new_count);\n\n        // Remove old failure-count labels before adding the new one.\n        // Each remove_label call is wrapped in a timeout.\n        for label in &labels {\n            if label.starts_with(\"failure-count:\") {\n                match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                    store.remove_label(&bead.id, label),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(())) => {}\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove old failure-count label\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            \"remove_label timed out after 30s\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add the new label with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, &new_label),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    count = new_count,\n                    \"failure count incremented\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add failure-count label\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"add_label timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(new_count)\n    }\n\n    /// Reset the failure count label on a bead by removing all `failure-count:N` labels.\n    ///\n    /// Called on success to clear the failure counter so the bead starts fresh\n    /// on the next cycle.\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn reset_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<()> {\n        // Read labels with timeout.\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(&bead.id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"could not read labels to reset failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, skipping failure count reset\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n            };\n\n        // Remove all failure-count labels.\n        let mut removed_count = 0;\n        for label in &labels {\n            if label.starts_with(\"failure-count:\") {\n                match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                    store.remove_label(&bead.id, label),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                        removed_count += 1;\n                    }\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove failure-count label\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            \"remove_label timed out after 30s\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if removed_count > 0 {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                removed_count,\n                \"failure count reset\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Quarantine a bead by setting status=blocked and adding the 'cycling' label.\n    ///\n    /// This is called when a bead exceeds the configured failure threshold.\n    /// Emits a BeadQuarantined telemetry event.\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn quarantine_bead(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        failure_count: u32,\n        threshold: u32,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<EventKind>> {\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            failure_count,\n            threshold,\n            \"quarantining bead after exceeding failure threshold\"\n        );\n\n        // Set status=blocked with timeout. This is what actually stops Pluck\n        // from re-selecting the bead — the 'cycling' label below is a\n        // human-facing marker, not the enforcement mechanism.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.block(&bead.id)).await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"set status=blocked\");\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to set status=blocked during quarantine\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"block\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"block timed out after 30s during quarantine\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"block\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add the 'cycling' label with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, \"cycling\"),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"added 'cycling' label\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add 'cycling' label\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"add_label timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Emit the BeadQuarantined event.\n        events.push(EventKind::BeadQuarantined {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            failure_count,\n            threshold,\n        });\n\n        Ok(events)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Outcome Display\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nimpl fmt::Display for Outcome {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Outcome::Success => write!(f, \"Success\"),\n            Outcome::Failure => write!(f, \"Failure\"),\n            Outcome::Timeout => write!(f, \"Timeout\"),\n            Outcome::AgentNotFound => write!(f, \"AgentNotFound\"),\n            Outcome::Interrupted => write!(f, \"Interrupted\"),\n            Outcome::Crash(code) => write!(f, \"Crash({})\", code),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::bead_store::Filters;\n    use .lock()\n                .unwrap()\n                .push(StoreAction::Block(id.to_string()));\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        async fn flush(&self) -> Result<()> {\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        async fn reopen(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n            self.actions\n                .lock()\n                .unwrap()\n                .push(StoreAction::Reopen(id.to_string()));\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        async fn labels(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n            Ok(self.labels.clone())\n        }\n        async fn add_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()> {\n            self.actions\n                .lock()\n                .unwrap()\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n///\n/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Outcome {\n    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n    Success,\n    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n    Failure,\n    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n    Timeout,\n    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n    AgentNotFound,\n    /// Exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) — agent was interrupted.\n    Interrupted,\n    /// Negative exit code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n    Crash(i32),\n}\n\nimpl Outcome {\n    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n    ///\n    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n    ///\n    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - all other → `Failure`\n    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n        if was_interrupted {\n            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n        }\n\n        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n        match exit_code {\n            // Success\n            0 => Outcome::Success,\n            // Explicit failure code\n            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n            // Failure range: 2-123\n            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionMode\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n///\n/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n///   and consecutive failure count.\n///\n/// # When to use each mode\n///\n/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n///\n/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n///\n/// # API boundary\n///\n/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n/// activated. No other code should check timeout status or exit codes to make\n/// this decision — all decomposition logic should route through this enum.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum DecompositionMode {\n    /// Timeout-driven decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// Contains timeout-specific context for use in generating child bead\n    /// proposals (e.g., original timeout value, elapsed time, progress indicators).\n    Timeout {\n        /// The timeout duration that was exceeded (in seconds).\n        timeout_seconds: u64,\n        /// Optional hint about what phase was being worked on when timeout occurred.\n        /// This can be used to name the first child bead (e.g., \"Phase 1: Routing Rules\").\n        current_phase_hint: Option<String>,\n    },\n    /// Ordinary failure mode — no decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Used for all non-timeout failures where splitting the bead into child\n    /// beads would not help. The bead should be retried, released, or escalated\n    /// via the normal failure-handling path.\n    OrdinaryFailure,\n}\n\nimpl DecompositionMode {\n    /// Returns true if this is timeout decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the decomposition path.\n    /// All code that needs to know whether to decompose should call this method\n    /// rather than inspecting the enum directly.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(mode.is_timeout());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_timeout());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_timeout(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::Timeout { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this is ordinary failure mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the normal failure\n    /// handling path (retry, release, or escalate without decomposition).\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_ordinary_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the timeout duration if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the timeout value without\n    /// pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), Some(120));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn timeout_seconds(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => Some(*timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the current phase hint if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the optional phase hint\n    /// without pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode\n    /// or when the hint is not set.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), Some(&\"Phase 1\".to_string()));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn current_phase_hint(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                current_phase_hint, ..\n            } => current_phase_hint.as_ref(),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DecompositionMode {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => write!(f, \"timeout ({}s)\", timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => write!(f, \"ordinary_failure\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandError {\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    ConfigError(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n    WorkCreated,\n    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n    NoWork,\n    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n    Error(StrandError),\n    /// The strand was skipped because its prerequisites are not met.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"ran and found nothing\")\n    /// and `Error` (which means \"ran but failed\"). `Skipped` means \"did not\n    /// run because the environment doesn't support it\" — e.g., a strand that\n    /// requires a home bead store when the worker is configured without one.\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n    /// Candidates were found but all were excluded/assigned — short retry needed.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"truly no candidates\").\n    /// `FoundButExcluded` means \"candidates exist but this worker can't claim\n    /// them right now\" — they're assigned to other workers or blocked by labels.\n    /// This signals the worker to use short retry backoff instead of long idle.\n    FoundButExcluded,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ClaimResult / ClaimOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a single claim attempt for one bead.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum ClaimResult {\n    /// This worker successfully claimed the bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Another worker claimed the bead first.\n    RaceLost {\n        /// Assignee that won the race.\n        claimed_by: String,\n    },\n    /// The bead cannot be claimed (not open, blocked, etc.).\n    NotClaimable {\n        /// Human-readable reason.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// Claim CLI failed with a store/CLI error (distinct from race-lost).\n    ClaimError {\n        /// Human-readable error message.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Aggregate outcome after exhausting all candidates for a selection cycle.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\npub enum ClaimOutcome {\n    /// Successfully claimed a bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Raced every candidate and lost every time.\n    AllRaceLost,\n    /// The strand returned no candidates.\n    NoCandidates,\n    /// The bead store returned an error.\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BrDependency\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A bead dependency as returned from the `br`/`bf` JSON output, or from\n/// bead-rs's `bead` (`{\"blocker\": \"<id>\", \"kind\": \"blocks\"}` — a lean\n/// edge-only shape with no enriched title/status/priority). The aliases\n/// below accept both without changing how bf/br JSON deserializes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct BrDependency {\n    #[serde(alias = \"blocker\")]\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub title: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub status: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    #[serde(rename = \"dependency_type\", alias = \"kind\", default)]\n    pub dependency_type: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?;\n    Ok(s.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()))\n}\n\n/// A comment on a bead.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Comment {\n    /// Comment ID (internal database ID).\n    pub id: i64,\n    /// The bead this comment is on.\n    #[serde(rename = \"issue_id\")]\n    pub bead_id: String,\n    /// The comment text.\n    pub text: String,\n    /// Author who created the comment.\n    pub author: String,\n    /// When the comment was created.\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n/// A bead as returned from the bead store.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Bead {\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Stored as `description` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"description\")]\n    pub body: Option<String>,\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    pub status: BeadStatus,\n    /// br emits `\"\"` for unassigned beads; normalize to `None`.\n    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = \"empty_string_as_none\")]\n    pub assignee: Option<String>,\n    /// br may omit this field when empty.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Stored as `source_repo` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"source_repo\", default)]\n    pub workspace: std::path::PathBuf,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependencies: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependents: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    /// Comments on this bead, returned by `bf show --json`.\n    /// Empty array if no comments or backend doesn't support comments.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub comments: Vec<Comment>,\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    // br ready --json omits updated_at; default to now so explore can deserialize it\n    #[serde(default = \"chrono::Utc::now\")]\n    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// AgentOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Raw output from an agent process (before outcome classification).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentOutcome {\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    pub stdout: String,\n    pub stderr: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Deserialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"method\", rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum InputMethod {\n    /// Write the prompt to the agent's stdin.\n    Stdin,\n    /// Write the prompt to a temp file and      /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(100, false), Outcome::Failure); // NOT timeout per spec\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(123, false), Outcome::Failure);\n        // 125-126 -> Failure (not assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(-1, false), Outcome::Crash(-1));\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(-9, false), Outcome::Crash(-9));\n        // Large positive values >255 -> Crash per spec (exit > Callers should treat timeout and error as non-fatal — log\n    /// and continue rather than blocking the worker in HANDLING state.\n    async fn timeout_op<T, F, Fut>(\n        &self,\n        op: F,\n        operation_name: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Option<T>, anyhow::Error>\n    where\n        F: FnOnce() -> Fut,\n        Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, anyhow::Error>>,\n    {\n        match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), op()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(result)) => Ok(Some(result)),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(e),\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    operation = operation_name,\n                    \"bead store operation timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Release a bead with sync conflict recovery and graceful failure handling.\n    ///\n    /// Flow:\n    /// 1. 1: Flush local writes to JSONL before attempting release.\n        // Emit heartbeat before br call to track where hang occurs.\n        let _ = self.timeout_op(|| store.flush(), \"flush\").await {\n            Ok(Some(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"flushed local changes to JSONL before release\"\n                );\n                // Emit heartbeat after successful flush.\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {\n                    bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),\n                    state: \"HANDLING_FLUSH_DONE\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"release\".to_string(),\n                    operation:                 state: \"HANDLING_RELEASE_DONE\".to_string(),\n                });\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n
